pr_title: Load playlist panels on demand to reduce initial load time when joining a room
pr_body:
- [x] Depends on #15878 
- Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/15829.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/144034804-8f2e243f-f2c3-48d6-8b1d-a0b5e1938851.mp4

Kudos to @bdach for some of the work in this PR.
pr_comments: Both cases should be better now. Opted to remove the populate function as it seems like it will be a pain point as long as it is public exposed.
Unsure how/why tests are failing. Debugger won't hook the exception and can't immediately see how it can even happen. Looks specifically related to `TestMultiplayerClient` somehow..

I've managed to ascertain that the `TeamVersus` test failures only occur if `TestChangeTypeViaMatchSettings` is ran in conjunction with another test (like e.g. `TestChangeTeamsViaButton`), and the immediate cause of the nullref is that the playlist item looks very uninitialised, including `Beatmap.Value` in particular:

![2021-12-01-224723_2013x800_scrot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20418176/144319320-faa2b7af-a019-4ceb-92f9-a0b7b38d3a58.png)

I don't have much more time left to investigate further today, unfortunately.
Thanks for that. I'm not sure how or why, but my rider refuses to break on that exception. Makes it very hard to investigate this one.

Turns out that the test failures were due to the drawable playlist item trying to populate the beatmap, even though one was already given synchronously, and writing back a null value when that request failed. I've fixed that with b3b239c, which turns off that lookup if the beatmap is populated, which feels like something we want anyhow (for when the beatmap is pre-populated, and second & subsequent loads).

That class needs to be split up some more to be less condition-y but that's probably out of scope here.

issue_context.title: Joining multiplayer rooms with multiple queue items is slow
issue_context.body: Looks to not join until sequential calls to `beatmapsets/lookup` complete for every item in the room.
comments: Definitely sounds bad, but I'm not super sure what the fix is there either. Should the items be allowed to load one by one, starting from the current item backwards? Or should there be a web endpoint for multiple lookups at once?
They should load as they come on screen, I think (probably using an async load/unload wrapper).

So I've spent a bit on trying to make async load work and I'm not sure it's viable. The thing is that the playlist item fetch is wedged quite deep in the multiplayer client and many things look to depend on it being synchronously populated.

I had limited "success" with the following branch: https://github.com/ppy/osu/compare/master...bdach:multiplayer-delayed-playlist-load-broken?expand=1 - while the happy path seems to mostly behave, it quickly broke down under me trying to stress the robustness of that solution against delayed loads/races:

![2021-11-27-141406_2556x1034_scrot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20418176/143683019-430b700f-5efd-4b31-9c0d-73c51e01b698.png)

(note the completely different: current map display on the top, difficulty rating spread display, and the playlist itself).
Temporarily assigning this one as I'm going to give it a shot (building off @bdach's existing work towards it).

> So I've spent a bit on trying to make async load work and I'm not sure it's viable. The thing is that the playlist item fetch is wedged quite deep in the multiplayer client and many things look to depend on it being synchronously populated.

While your approach here might alleviate the immediate delay, it's still potentially going to result in thousands of API requests being queued up on joining a room, which are hanging and never cancelled even after leaving the room, and will hold up all other game-wide operations. Maybe one step better than what we have, but also not really solving the full problem.

I still think that population should only happen when the drawable panels come on screen. Will see if I can make that happen. I can understand how this is a struggle with the way multiplayer is structured client-side. It's very very very complex. And these items are used anywhere and everywhere.

review_comments:
Unfortunately this drawable is shared with playlists (the mode), and also used in places wherein this fetch doesn't need to happen. For instance it will run on the room creation screen before anything online has happened yet.

The immediate simplest way to counteract this would be to add local guards (`showItemOwner && Item.OwnerID > 0`, `Item.Beatmap.Value != null`). But the time is rapidly approaching wherein this component needs to be split into multiple ones, this one implementation is approaching critical mass wrt what it can do.
Hmm, I did test this not to break that scenario. The code path already checks whether the beatmap is already populated and early aborts.

Oh, right, the beatmap fetch will be a no-op lower down, sure. I forgot about that. But there's still the issue of the user fetch (happens even if owner id is 0 / owner is not shown on playlist), and in general the fact that playlist item panels in playlists mode are now calling things from `MultiplayerClient` at all is pretty weird.

Yeah, for sure. I don't think this is the correct PR to be doing larger refactors there (will probably conflict with @smoogipoo's ongoing work on the queue display).

I'll fix the user lookup part.

There is one slight visual issue here that I haven't fixed on my proof-of-concept branch and remains here too, namely that the late-populated beatmaps don't update the star rating range. This would be easy enough to fix if `BindableList` had a `TriggerChange()` call, but it doesn't (and trying to fix the "naive" way by assigning the changed item to self kerploded on me in some arcane way).

The range isn't too important to fix right now as we are changing the way that works (the initial range should be sent from the server as two numbers).

Also needs consideration as to whether it should include expired items in the first place, for example.
